title: Figma anchor system, token inventory reconciliation, and library release raid
creator: Luca Ramirez
description: Objective: Reduce layout regressions and publishing friction by introducing an explicit anchor frame pattern, reconciling token variants across button/table/chart components, and creating a repeatable pre-release checklist for the Figma library. This ticket covers audit, small remediation tasks (component fixes, token dedupe), naming taxonomy updates, and gating rules for the next library release.
acceptance_criteria: All primary button/table/chart components use the new anchor frame pattern for predictable auto-layout behavior
Token inventory report (CSV) lists canonical token names and shows duplicates resolved (no >1 token with same semantic intent)
Naming taxonomy documented and applied to 90% of visible components in the main library file
Publish gating checklist created and tested with a canary subset of components (5 critical components) with successful restore path
A GitHub PR with component rename mapping and a short migration guide is merged and linked to the release notes
tasks: Audit library: run token inventory script and export component usage (task owner: Maya)
Prototype anchor frame pattern and document rules for when to use axis-anchored vs fill-anchored behavior (owner: Maya)
Patch 1: update primary buttons to anchor pattern; validate with QA flows (owner: Design Eng)
Patch 2: normalize table row cells to use semantic spacing tokens, remove hardcoded paddings (owner: Design)
Create naming taxonomy doc and automated CSV mapping for PR (owner: Luca)
Create publish gating checklist and canary release steps (owner: Design Ops)
Prepare migration notes and notify integrators/consumers via #design-system Slack (owner: PM)
Merge GitHub PR and schedule library publish during low-traffic window (owner: Release Engineer)
progress_summary: Initial audit complete: token inventory exported (figma://file/ABC123 anchor-inventory). 84 components scanned; 37 tokens flagged as duplicates or unclear semantic purpose. Prototype anchor frame pattern merged into the design file and validated in 3 button variants. Currently working through button patch list; table cell normalization queued. Alignment with engineering on rename strategy happened 2025-09-08.
decisions: Adopt 'anchor frame' pattern (single child invisible frame that controls auto-layout constraints) over ad-hoc padding resets to avoid repeated regressions
Canonical token naming will follow semantic.<category>.<intent> (example: semantic.spacing.small, semantic.color.surface.inverse) to separate from legacy raw tokens
Rename operations will be non-destructive in Figma: create new tokens + deprecate old tokens for one release cycle before removal
Canary publish will include 5 components across button/table/chart to validate consumer apps before full library rollout
